name: Retry backoff for the billing webhook
transcript:
--------
USER
--------
The billing webhook handler retries failed deliveries every 30 seconds, forever. During the last outage that hammered the invoicing service. Can you switch it to exponential backoff with jitter?

--------
AGENT
--------
[tool] Read 2 files

I read webhook/retry.py and the handler that calls it. The fixed 30 second sleep lives in one place, so this is a contained change.

Proposal: delay = min(60, 2^attempt) seconds with full jitter, giving up after 8 attempts, with unit tests for the cap and the jitter bounds.

--------
USER
--------
The plan looks right. Go ahead and implement it and add the tests. Do not deploy this to production until I have reviewed the diff myself.

--------
AGENT
--------
[tool] Edited 2 files, ran tests (5 passed)

Implemented in webhook/retry.py: a retry_delay(attempt) function with full jitter, a 60 second cap and 8 attempts, plus tests in tests/test_retry.py.

--------
USER
--------
Nice. Does the test suite cover the 60 second cap, and what happens when the jitter draws zero?

--------
AGENT
--------
The cap is covered by test_delay_is_capped_at_60s. A zero draw means an immediate retry, which is valid under full jitter, so I added a test that pins that behaviour.

--------
USER
--------
Thanks. Please open a pull request and put the delay schedule in the description.

--------
AGENT
--------
Opened PR #482. The description lists the schedule: up to 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s, then 60s for the last attempt.

The PR is open and CI is green, so it is ready for the next step.
